main_text.head: LIBER TERTIVS. DE SENATV QVINGENTORVM ET CONCIONE.
TITVLVS PRIMVS.
main_text.p: CUM eruditissime à praestantissimis viris de Quingentorum Senatu disputatum sit, ne, quod aiunt, actum agere videamur, pauca tantum delibabimus, quae omnino necessaria sunt ad hunc, quem de illo Senatu instituimus, sermonem.

Constituit Solon, ut quotannis summae praeesset Reipublicae Quadringentorum Senatus, non ducto e variis ordinibus numero, quod olim volebat Plato Lib. VI. de Legibus, id quippe denegatum Solonis Legibus [illegible, ~12 letters] vt in hunc Senatum allegerentur: [illegible, ~30 letters], neque postea quoque, aucto numero, concessum, sed e quatuor Tribubus. Plutarchus in Solone: [illegible, ~40 letters] Quadringentis facti sunt Quingenti Senatores, qui dicti sunt [illegible, ~10 letters] βουλὴ, aut οἱ Πεντακόσιοι. Ex vnaquaque enim Tribu quinginti viri sorte ducebantur: [illegible, ~25 letters], inquit Vlpianus in Androtianam, [illegible, ~20 letters]. Sortiebantur autem, qui aetate essent Senatoria. Libanius in Hypothesi Androtianae: [illegible, ~35 letters].

Aetatem Senatoriam definitam fuisse puto anno tricesimo: Oportet namque tot annos natum fuisse ludicem, vt constat ex Heliastarum iureiurando: ΚΑΙ ΓΕΓΟΝΑ ΟΥΚ ΕΛΑΤΤΟΝ Η ΤΡΙΑΚΟΝΤΑ ΕΤΗ. Quingenti autem hi etiam inter iudices: nam vere Plato Lib. VI. de Legibus, [illegible, ~20 letters]. Praeterea hoc Senatu moti poterant forte capi in iudices, vt legimus in Graecorum Commentariis [illegible, ~45 letters]. page.notes: Greek passages are only partly legible at this scan resolution. Where I could not read the Greek letter by letter I have marked it illegible rather than guess. The Greek in the Heliastarum oath line (ΚΑΙ ΓΕΓΟΝΑ ΟΥΚ ΕΛΑΤΤΟΝ Η ΤΡΙΑΚΟΝΤΑ ΕΤΗ) is printed in capitals and is reproduced as I read it. The woodcut initial C is joined to CUM. The page ends mid-word at "Tri-" with a printed hyphen; no catchword is visible. The ornamental header and the Google watermark at the foot are not transcribed.
